rationale: Each of these at-rules DECLARES a named, referable thing, so each publishes a symbol and each use of it is an edge whose BOTH endpoints resolve — the same both-ends-must-resolve rule the chain, animation and font-family edges follow. `@custom-media` publishes the bare `--ident` and NOT `@custom-media --narrow (max-width: 400px)`, for the same reason `@property` publishes `--brand` and not `@property --brand`: the name is the referable part, the condition is its value. That also means a `@custom-media` symbol and a registered `@property` symbol are the same SHAPE, so each carries a metadata marker saying which construct declared it. `@font-feature-settings` is emitted ONLY inside a `@font-face`: a rule-level one is legal CSS, but which family's feature it names depends on the cascade, and emitting an edge there would invent an endpoint for something this lane cannot see — so the rule-level use in this fixture is deliberately the forbidden one.
_targetSpelling: CSS-D15: a target that names a declaration THIS file publishes is spelled `<file-scope>::<name>`, where the scope is the file's project-relative path without its extension. The bare spelling stays for a target this file does not declare (a cross-file or external reference) and for `imports`, whose target is another file's module name.
